q: 196. The floor which is best for recommendation in heavy industries, warehouses etc. is
explain: Granolithic flooring uses hard-wearing aggregates like granite to create a surface that can withstand heavy impacts and machinery.

q: 197. The thickness of Asphalt floor varies from
explain: Asphalt mastic flooring is typically laid in a thickness of 25mm to 40mm for standard wear and tear.

q: 198. The wedge shaped bricks or blocks used for the construction of an arch are called as
options: none of a, b and c
explain: Voussoirs are the tapered units that make up the curve of an arch; the center-most voussoir is specifically called the keystone.

q: 199. Batching error means in accuracy in the quantity of
explain: Batching is the process of measuring all concrete ingredients; an error in any of these affects the final strength and workability.

q: 200. The upper convex surface of an arch is called as
explain: The extrados is the outer (upper) curved line of an arch, while the intrados is the inner curve.

q: 201. The irregular triangular portion of the arcade, formed between the two arches is called as
explain: Spandrils are the triangular spaces found between adjacent arches or between an arch and a rectangular enclosure.

q: 202. The inclined supports provided in an arch constructed to receive the arch are called as
explain: A skewback is the inclined surface on an abutment from which an arch rises.

q: 203. When rise of an arch is more than half of span of the arch and its lower portion is straight instead of circular, then it is called as
explain: A stilted arch has vertical 'stilts' below the curve, making the total height greater than half the span.

q: 204. When rise of an arch is more than the span, then the arch is called as
explain: Lancet arches are very tall and narrow pointed arches, where the rise significantly exceeds the span.

q: 205. In any case of the bearing of a lintel should not be less than
explain: The minimum structural bearing (overlap) for a lintel onto a wall is standardly 10 cm to ensure load distribution.

q: 206. Flat roof are particularly suitable for tropical places because
options: The top of the flat proof can be used as a terrace
All of the above are correct
explain: In tropics, flat roofs provide outdoor space, help regulate heat through thermal mass, and allow for easy future expansion.

q: 207. Pitched roofs are particularly suitable in hilly regions because
options: It is very easy to repair
of heavy rain fall and snow fall
all of the above are correct
explain: Steep slopes allow rain and snow to shed quickly, preventing structural overload from snow accumulation.

q: 208. The pitched roof which slopes in all the four directions is named as
explain: A hip roof has slopes on all four sides which meet at the corners to form hips.

q: 209. The members laid horizontally to support the common rafters and to transmit the load to the trusses walls are called as
explain: Purlins are horizontal beams that span between trusses to support the roof rafters or sheeting.

q: 210. The short piece of timber bolted to the rafters of a roof truss fixing the purlins in position are named as
explain: Cleats are small blocks used to prevent purlins from sliding or tilting on the rafters.

q: 211. For a span ranging in between 3.5 m to 4.5 m the most suitable type of roof is
explain: A couple-close roof adds a horizontal tie to prevent the rafters from spreading, making it suitable for mid-range spans.

q: 212. For a span ranging in between 6 m to 9 m, the most suitable type of pitched roof is
explain: The King Post truss is the most efficient design for spans up to 9 meters.

q: 213. The inclined braces used in a truss to prevent the sagging of the principal rafters are called as
explain: Struts are compression members in a truss that support the principal rafters and prevent them from bending.

q: 214. In asbestos cement corrugated sheet roofing, and minimum horizontal lap in metres should be
explain: A 150mm (0.15m) end lap is required to ensure the roof remains watertight during wind-driven rain.

q: 215. Arches over openings are preferred to lintel beams when
options: loads are heavy and span is large
explain: Arches are superior to lintels for wide spans and heavy loads because they act in compression, provided strong supports are present.

q: 216. Brick lintels are used when the span is
explain: Plain brick lintels have very low tensile strength and are restricted to spans of 1 meter or less.

q: 217. The angle of the skewback with the horizontal in the case of flat arches is usually
explain: For flat (camber) arches, the skewbacks are traditionally cut at a 60-degree angle.

q: 218. The lower half of the arch between the crown and the skewback is known as
explain: The haunch is the middle portion of the arch between the crown (top) and the springing (base).

q: 219. The projected portion of the tread (which is usually rounded) beyond the face of the riser is
explain: This is a repeat of the definition for nosing; it enhances the effective width of the tread.

q: 220. A vertical member supporting the hand rail is known as
explain: Balusters are the smaller vertical members that support the handrail and fill the space between the tread and the rail.

q: 221. In domestic buildings, the sufficient widths of the stair is about
explain: For residential or domestic buildings, a width of 0.9m (approx. 3 feet) is considered sufficient for comfortable movement.

q: 222. In public buildings the widths of the steps may be kept between
explain: Public buildings require wider stairs (1.5m to 1.8m) to accommodate higher foot traffic and emergency exit requirements.

q: 223. Normally the rise of the steps would be
explain: A riser height of 10cm to 15cm is standard for comfortable climbing, especially in public infrastructure.

q: 224. The normal tread length varies between
explain: A tread length (going) of 25cm to 30cm ensures the full foot has enough surface area to land safely.

q: 225. A stair in which all the steps are winders is
explain: In a spiral stair, all steps radiate from a central post and are tapered (winders).

q: 226. A stair which changes its direction by 180° is
explain: Half-turn stairs, such as dog-legged stairs, involve two flights that reverse direction by 180 degrees.

q: 227. Dog-legged stair is a
explain: The dog-legged stair is the most common type of half-turn stair where the two flights are contiguous with no well between them.

q: 228. How many treads would be there in a straight stair connecting two floors with height difference of 3.6 m? The rise is 15 cm.
explain: Total risers = 360/15 = 24. Since treads = Risers - 1 for a single flight, the answer is 23.

q: 229. How many treads would be there in a dog-legged stair connecting two floor with a height difference of 3.6 m? The rise of the steps is 15 cm.
explain: In a dog-legged stair with two flights, each flight has 12 risers and 11 treads. Total treads = 11 + 11 = 22.

q: 230. A roof which slopes in all the four directions is
explain: A hip roof has slopes on all four sides which meet at the corners to form hips.

q: 231. A roof which slopes in two directions is knows as
explain: A gable roof consists of two sloping surfaces meeting at a ridge, forming a triangle at the ends.

q: 232. A roof which slopes in all four directions and having flat top is known as
explain: A deck roof is similar to a hip roof but the top portion is kept flat for use as a terrace.

q: 233. The horizontal wooden or steel members which support the common rafter in a truss are called
explain: Purlins are horizontal members spanning between trusses to support the rafters or roofing sheets.

q: 234. The number of vertical posts in a queen post truss
explain: A Queen Post truss is characterized by having exactly two vertical tension members (posts).

q: 235. Queen-post trusses are used when the span is
explain: Queen post trusses are economical and suitable for spans ranging from 8 to 12 meters.

q: 236. Joining two wooden members at an angle is known as
explain: Mitring is the process of joining two pieces of wood at an angle, usually 45 degrees, to form a corner.

q: 237. In doors and windows, style is
options: the vertical member of the frame
the vertical member of the shutter
the member which divides the frame into two vertical portions
explain: Styles are the outermost vertical members of a door or window shutter.

q: 238. The horizontal members of the shutter of a door or window are called
explain: Rails are the horizontal structural members of a shutter, such as top, lock, and bottom rails.

q: 239. The normal height of the door in residential buildings
explain: A standard door height for residential buildings is typically 2.0 meters (approx 6'7").

q: 240. The thickness of shutter of the door generally does not exceed
explain: Standard internal wooden door shutters are usually 30mm thick.

q: 241. The sill window in residential buildings is generally kept above the floor level by
explain: A window sill height of 80cm (approx 32 inches) is standard for safety and furniture placement.

q: 242. In the battened and ledged door, the vertical wooden boards are called
explain: Battens are the vertical boards; they are secured by horizontal ledges.

q: 243. The type of door used when good ventilation is required in the room and at the same time privacy is maintained
explain: Louvered doors have slanted slats that allow air through while obstructing direct vision.

q: 244. Grade of concrete generally not used in RCC is
explain: M10 is a lean mix used for levelling or mud mats, not for structural reinforced concrete.

q: 245. A semi-rigid material ideally suited to make damp proof course is
explain: Mastic asphalt is a semi-rigid, durable material highly effective for preventing dampness.

q: 246. The complete dislocation of some portion of plastered surface due to imperfect bond resulting in patches is known as
explain: Peeling occurs when the plaster does not adhere to the surface and comes off in chunks or patches.

q: 247. In cinema theaters, to avoid reverberation, the longitudinal walls should be
explain: Walls that converge toward the screen help manage sound reflections and prevent echo.

q: 248. The volume of space per person to be provided in cinema theatres for good acoustics is
explain: Optimal acoustic performance in theaters requires a specific volume (3.7 - 4.2 m2/person) to control sound absorption.

q: 249. The comfortable temperature range in summer may be generally taken as
explain: Human thermal comfort in summer is generally achieved between 20°C and 23°C.

q: 250. The sound will be painful to the ear when its intensity exceeds
explain: 130 decibels is considered the threshold of pain for the human ear.

q: 251. Codes used in Nepal for building construction/ design is
explain: Nepal follows its own National Building Code (NBC) for structural design and safety.

q: 252. The foundations are placed below ground level, to increase
explain: Embedding foundations below ground level provides lateral support and prevents sliding, increasing stability.

q: 253. Dado is usually provided in
explain: Dado is a protective wall lining (usually tile) provided in bathrooms to prevent water damage.

q: 254. The foundation in which a cantilever beam is provided to join two footings, is known as
explain: A strap footing uses a connecting beam (strap) to distribute loads between an eccentrically loaded footing and an interior one.

q: 255. The process of making the back ground rough, before plastering, is
explain: Hacking involves creating small grooves in a smooth concrete surface to improve plaster adhesion.

q: 256. Black cotton soil is unsuitable for foundations because its
options: property to undergo a volumetric change due to variation of moisture content
explain: Black cotton soil swells significantly when wet and shrinks when dry, which can cause foundation failure.

q: 257. A double timber floor consists of
explain: In double timber floors, bridging joists are supported by binders to reduce the span and thickness.

q: 258. The exterior angle between outer faces of a wall, is known as
explain: A quoin is the external angle or corner of a building wall.

q: 259. A projecting piece usually provided to support a truss, is
explain: A cornice is a decorative and functional horizontal projection at the top of a wall.

q: 260. The line of intersection of the surfaces of a sloping roof forming an external angle exceeding 180°, is
explain: A hip is the external angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof surfaces.
